verses.author: model_A
verses.text: A boat leaves the harbor before anyone is awake to see it go.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left coffee cooling on the sill,
already forgetting whose hands made it warm.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Fog erases the shoreline first,
then the gulls, then the sound of the gulls,
until only the smell of salt remains.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone counts the buoys by memory alone,
numbers surfacing before the shapes do,
a small arithmetic against the white.

a note left unread beside the door,

verses.text:
Someone is teaching a child to whistle,
breath scattering before the note can land,
the porch steps littered with small failures.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The child tries again, cheeks puffed like sails,
and one note finally clears the railing,
thin as a thread pulled taut into the fog.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone else opens the note by the door at last,
the ink long dried, the words gone stubborn,
a whole winter folded into one line.
